citeAs: Hauret, J., Olivier, M., Joubaud, T., Langrenne, C., Poirée, S., Zimpfer, V., and Bavu, É. (2024). Vibravox: A Dataset of French Speech Captured with Body-conduction Audio Sensors. Submitted to Elsevier Speech Communication.
creator: Julien Hauret, Malo Olivier, Thomas Joubaud, Christophe Langrenne, Sarah Poirée, Véronique Zimpfer, Éric Bavu (Conservatoire national des arts et métiers / French-German Research Institute of Saint-Louis)
description: Vibravox is a GDPR-compliant dataset of French speech captured with five different body-conduction audio sensors (two in-ear microphones, two bone conduction vibration pickups, and a laryngophone) plus an airborne reference microphone. It contains 45 hours per sensor of speech samples and physiological sounds recorded by 188 participants under different acoustic conditions imposed by a high-order ambisonics 3D spatializer. The corpus includes four subsets (speech-clean, speech-noisy, speechless-clean, speechless-noisy) along with annotations about recording conditions and linguistic transcriptions.
name: Vibravox
publisher: Laboratoire de Mécanique des Structures et des Systèmes Couplés, Conservatoire national des arts et métiers (Cnam)
rai:annotatorDemographics: 188 participants (97 female, 91 male) contributed recordings. Female participants: mean age 25.9 years, median 22, range 19–59. Male participants: mean age 31.4 years, median 27, range 18–82. Overall: mean age 28.55 years, median 25, range 18–82. Participants were recruited with a deliberate effort for diversity and gender balance.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Phoneme Error Rate (PER) was computed for each sample using the Levenshtein distance between the labeled phonetic transcription and the phonetic transcription derived from Whisper's output. Samples with PER > 10% were discarded. Out of 200 participants and 30,568 initially collected sentences, 188 participants and 28,471 sentences were retained (6% of participants and 6.8% of sentences excluded).
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Text transcriptions were sourced from French Wikipedia (Common Voice subset) and filtered/normalized. Phonetic transcriptions were generated automatically using the CoML lab text phonemizer (IPA, 33 French phonemes), with manual phonetic transcription for words unrecognized by the phonemizer (e.g., "algorithme"). Recording condition annotations (subset labels, split assignments) were assigned based on the recording protocol steps.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset was deliberately designed to be gender-balanced and diverse: "a deliberate effort was made to recruit a diverse and gender-balanced group of participants." The dataset contains 97 female and 91 male speakers. Age distribution is skewed younger (mean 28.55 years, median 25, range 18–82). The dataset is exclusively French-language, which may limit generalizability to other languages. The noise recordings were sourced from AudioSet with focus on battlefield and industrial environments, which may not represent all real-world noise scenarios.
rai:dataCollection: 188 participants (out of 200 recruited) wore six audio sensors simultaneously and performed four recording steps: (1) reading sentences from French Wikipedia for 15 minutes (speech-clean), (2) remaining silent in a noisy environment for ~2.5 minutes (speechless-noisy), (3) remaining silent in complete silence for 54 seconds (speechless-clean), and (4) speaking in a noisy environment for 54 seconds (speech-noisy). Recordings were made in a 3D sound spatializer with a spherical array of 56 loudspeakers. The Zoom F8n field recorder captured all six sensor signals simultaneously at 48 kHz / 32 bits.
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Out of 200 participants, 12 were excluded after post-processing (6%). Out of 30,568 initially collected sentences, 2,097 were discarded (6.8%). Issues included mispronounced sentences, sensors shifting from initial positions, occasional sensor malfunctions, and microphones inadvertently left unequipped. Some participants had ear canals too small for the rigid in-ear microphone, which was not always caught by automatic filters.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Six simultaneous audio channels recorded at 48 kHz / 32-bit resolution using a Zoom F8n field recorder, with a 20 Hz high-pass filter applied to each acquisition channel. Sensors include: headset microphone (Shure WH20XLR), forehead accelerometer (Knowles BU23173-000), in-ear soft foam microphone (Knowles FG-23329-P07), in-ear rigid earpiece microphone (Knowles SPH1642HT5H), throat microphone (iXradio XVTM822D-D35), and temple vibration pickup (AKG C411).
rai:dataLimitations: The speech-noisy subset lacks a clean reference signal, limiting its use primarily to testing rather than training. Some participants had ear canals too small for the rigid in-ear microphone to achieve proper acoustic sealing, which was not always caught by the automatic filters. The temple vibration pickup has very limited bandwidth (below 1500 Hz), restricting its utility for high-frequency speech tasks. The dataset is exclusively in French, limiting cross-lingual applicability.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dataset is split by speaker: 80% of male and female speakers in training, 10% in validation, 10% in test, ensuring no speaker overlap between splits. VAD timestamps were extended by 0.6 seconds on both sides; audio trimmed by 15 ms if boundaries exceeded original audio. For noisy condition experiments (not part of the static dataset itself), speechless-noisy segments are dynamically mixed with speech-clean utterances to simulate noisy speech with a clean reference.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Text preprocessing: sentences from French Wikipedia filtered to remove proper names (except common first names, French town/region/country names), numbers, Greek letters, mathematical symbols, and syntactic errors; text normalized by lowercasing and removing punctuation except apostrophes; phonetic transcription generated using IPA with the CoML lab phonemizer, with manual correction for unrecognized words. Audio preprocessing: 20 Hz high-pass filter applied to all channels. Post-collection filtering: three automatic filters applied — (1) PER < 10% (Levenshtein distance between labeled and Whisper-derived phonetic transcription), (2) SNR[i,j] > 1.5 dB (speech vs. silence energy ratio per sensor), (3) Lspeech_50[i,j] > Lsilence_50[i] (sensitivity drift detection). VAD timestamps extended by 0.6 seconds on both sides; audio trimmed by 15 ms if boundaries exceeded.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to stimulate research in body-conducted speech capture for robust communication in noisy environments, with applications in military operations, industrial settings, and access control. The paper notes potential biometric applications including speaker identification for intelligence gathering and battlefield forensics. The dataset was designed to be GDPR-compliant, with informed consent, anonymization, and encryption of participant data.
rai:dataUseCases: Speech enhancement (bandwidth extension, joint denoising and bandwidth extension), speech recognition (speech-to-phonemes/text), speaker verification, voice commands development, vital sign monitoring (heart rate tracking), and research into body-conducted speech capture with non-conventional audio sensors. Intended for training and evaluating deep learning models for robust communication in noisy environments.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: whisper-timestamped (a speech-to-text engine based on OpenAI Whisper with dynamic time warping applied to cross-attention weights) was used for Voice Activity Detection and Phoneme Error Rate computation during post-processing filtering. The CoML lab text phonemizer was used for automatic phonetic transcription.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Voice recordings (biometric data) from 188 participants, including physiological sounds (breathing, swallowing, heart rate signals). The paper notes that body-conduction sensors capture rich biometric information including heart rate and breathing. All data was collected under GDPR compliance with informed consent, anonymization, and encryption.

null_reasons.rai:annotationsPerItem: The dataset uses automated annotation (phonemizer + Whisper) rather than multiple independent human annotators per item; no per-item annotation count is discussed.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: No annotation platform (e.g., MTurk, Label Studio) is mentioned; annotations were generated programmatically using the CoML phonemizer and whisper-timestamped tools.
null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: No imputation of missing values is described; defective samples were discarded rather than imputed.
null_reasons.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: No versioning, update cadence, or maintenance plan is described in the paper beyond the initial public release on HuggingFace.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: The paper only describes per-session durations (15 min, 2.5 min, 54 sec, 54 sec), not the overall calendar timeframe when data collection took place. No start/end dates are given.

evidence.name: Vibravox is a dataset compliant with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) containing audio recordings using five different body-conduction audio sensors
evidence.description: Vibravox is a dataset compliant with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) containing audio recordings using five different body-conduction audio sensors: two in-ear microphones, two bone conduction vibration pickups, and a laryngophone. The dataset also includes audio data from an airborne microphone used as a reference. The Vibravox corpus contains 45 hours per sensor of speech samples and physiological sounds recorded by 188 participants under different acoustic conditions imposed by a high order ambisonics 3D spatializer.

evidence.isLiveDataset: This highly curated dataset, comprising four subsets — speech-clean, speech-noisy, speechless-clean, and speechless-noisy — is now publicly available. The total duration of the 6-channel recordings is over 45 hours per sensor, with 188 participants.
evidence.rai:dataCollection: The recording process consists of four steps that are performed consecutively for each participant in the order listed below. Each of these steps corresponds to a subset of the Vibravox dataset. speech-clean: The participant reads sentences sourced from the French Wikipedia for a duration of 15 minutes. speechless-noisy: For a period of 2 minutes and 24 seconds, the subject is required to remain silent yet free to move, swallow, and breathe naturally in a noisy environment.
evidence.rai:dataCollectionType: Creating the Vibravox BCM dataset involved a number of different tasks. These included designing pre-amplification and conditioning circuits for each transducer, coding the front-end and back-end software for the recording user interface, adapting the housings and fixings for some audio sensors to the human body through 3D modeling and printing, and selecting transducer technologies and recording parameters.
evidence.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The Zoom F8n records all six sensor signals simultaneously, operates at a sampling rate of 48 kHz and a resolution of 32 bits, thereby guaranteeing precise signal capture with high fidelity. To enhance audio data quality, a 20 Hz high-pass filter is uniformly applied to each acquisition channel, effectively attenuating low-frequency noise and artifacts.
evidence.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: speech-clean: The participant reads sentences sourced from the French Wikipedia for a duration of 15 minutes. speechless-noisy: For a period of 2 minutes and 24 seconds, the subject is required to remain silent. speechless-clean: The procedure is repeated for 54 seconds in complete silence. speech-noisy: The final phase (54 seconds)
evidence.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The filtering process comprises two main stages. In the first stage, indicators for evaluating audio capture quality are extracted. The whisper-timestamped model constitutes a key component of our indicator extraction process. The first filter discards any audio samples where PER[j] > 10%. The second filter is employed to verify that the sensor is functioning correctly, specifically by examining the ratio between speech and silence energy levels on a given sample. The last filter is designed to detect any potential sensitivity drift on the sensors.
evidence.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: From this normalized text, we also generated the corresponding phonetic transcription using the International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA), which contains 33 phonemes in French. This operation was done with the text phonemizer of the CoML lab. For some words, the phonemizer produced some language switches that we wanted to avoid, to preserve the minimal French phonetic alphabet. A phase of manual phonetic transcription was then necessary for these unrecognized words, such as "algorithme".
evidence.rai:machineAnnotationTools: The whisper-timestamped model constitutes a key component of our indicator extraction process. This model is a speech-to-text engine based on Whisper that applies dynamic time warping to cross-attention weights. By aligning the transcription with the raw waveform, accurate prediction of word timestamps in speech segments can be used to identify sequences containing vocalizations.
evidence.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: PER[j]: Phoneme Error Rate is computed for each sample j using the Levenshtein distance between the phonetic labeled transcription and the phonetic transcription derived from Whisper's output. Out of 200 participants, 188 were retained, with a total of 28,471 sentences. Given that this post-processing filtering excluded a non-negligible amount of data (6% of participants and 6.8% of pronounced sentences)
evidence.rai:dataUseCases: The Vibravox dataset offers considerable potential across various applications, particularly in improving communication in noisy environments. Furthermore, the Vibravox dataset displays potential for applications such as developing voice commands and monitoring vital signs, including heart rate, particularly when utilizing the speechless-clean subset.
evidence.rai:dataSocialImpact: In accordance with the guidelines of the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), which governs the processing and protection of personal data of citizens and residents of the European Union (EU), all necessary measures were taken to protect the privacy and rights of participants in this study. This included obtaining informed consent, clearly communicating the purpose of data collection, and ensuring anonymization and encryption of data during storage and analysis.
evidence.rai:dataLimitations: However, in some cases, such as when a participant's ear canal was too small for the rigid in-ear microphone to achieve proper acoustic sealing, these filters were not triggered. The speech-noisy subset is of particular interest for showcasing the noise-resilient capabilities of BCMs. However, this subset primarily serves testing purposes, as it lacks a clean reference under such conditions.
evidence.rai:dataBiases: To increase the representativeness and inclusivity of the dataset, a deliberate effort was made to recruit a diverse and gender-balanced group of participants. The dataset is then split by speaker, with 80% of male and female speakers in the training set, 10% in the development/validation set, and 10% in the test set.

evidence.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Beyond this paper's focus, this rich biometric data (heart rate, breathing) could be a game-changer in battlefield forensics, aiding in revealing emotional states and tracking life signals during critical events. In accordance with the guidelines of the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), all necessary measures were taken to protect the privacy and rights of participants in this study. This included obtaining informed consent, clearly communicating the purpose of data collection, and ensuring anonymization and encryption of data during storage and analysis.
evidence.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: A total of J=30,568 sentences were initially collected from 200 participants in the speech-clean subset. However, a small number of audio clips had various shortcomings: although we carefully monitored and validated each recording during the experimental process, the workflow was not entirely foolproof. Mispronounced sentences, sensors shifting from their initial positions, occasional sensor malfunctions, or instances where a microphone was inadvertently left unequipped led to some data inconsistencies.
evidence.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dataset is then split by speaker, with 80% of male and female speakers in the training set, 10% in the development/validation set, and 10% in the test set. This ensures that all utterances from a given speaker are grouped together, preventing any speaker overlap between splits.
